findings.claim: The restored-delivery scenario does not actually force delivery back on, so an ambient FRF_DISABLE_DELIVERY=1 makes acceptance A fail even after the runner's intended restoration step.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 3 requires "disabling delivery makes that assertion fail before restoration passes," but run_required_test only sets FRF_DISABLE_DELIVERY=1 for mode disabled and runs the enabled branch as `"${command[@]}"`, inheriting any pre-existing FRF_DISABLE_DELIVERY from the caller.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the enabled scenario with FRF_DISABLE_DELIVERY explicitly unset, e.g. `env -u FRF_DISABLE_DELIVERY "${command[@]}"`, or reject caller-provided FRF_DISABLE_DELIVERY at startup.

findings.claim: The readiness check only verifies that the Iggy TCP port accepts connections, which can race the service becoming protocol-ready and make the integration runner flaky.
findings.evidence: wait_for_iggy uses a Node net.createConnection probe and exits on TCP connect, then main immediately runs the gateway test against Iggy; acceptance requires a reliable local fixture proving publish/subscription delivery.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the raw TCP probe with an Iggy protocol/API readiness check or retry `IggyBroker::new`/channel creation until the existing deadline expires.
